title: Anxiety and anxiety disorders
summary: Describes anxiety disorders, their causes and symptoms, when to seek help, ways to reduce anxiety and the main types of anxiety disorders.

atoms.title: What an anxiety disorder is
atoms.question: What is an anxiety disorder?
atoms.text: An anxiety disorder is defined as having racing thoughts or feelings paralyzed by fear, or when thoughts feel out of control. Anxiety may at times be a healthy emotion that alerts you to pay better attention to your mental health, but when intrusive what-if worries start to affect daily life, you may have an anxiety disorder. More than 40 million adults in the United States are affected.
questions: When does anxiety become a disorder?

atoms.title: What causes anxiety
atoms.question: What causes anxiety?
atoms.text: The exact cause of anxiety is unknown, but research points to genetic factors and negative events or stressful life experiences playing a role. Some health conditions or medication side effects may also produce or aggravate symptoms. Anxiety can happen as a reaction to relationships, health, school, work, finances, unexpected changes or big life events.

atoms.title: Signs and symptoms of an anxiety disorder
atoms.question: What are the symptoms of an anxiety disorder?
atoms.text: Signs and symptoms of an anxiety disorder may include thoughts that won't go away, a hard time focusing, avoiding situations out of worry, using alcohol, drugs or tobacco to cope, eating more or less than usual, a sense of danger or doom, feeling nervous, restless, weak or fatigued, increased heart rate, fast breathing, headaches, muscle pain, trouble sleeping, stomach pain, and dizziness.
questions: What does an anxiety disorder feel like?

atoms.title: When to seek professional help for anxiety
atoms.question: When should I seek professional help for anxiety?
atoms.text: If you are experiencing the signs of anxiety listed, it may be time to get help; finding a mental health provider is an important first step. You may also consider mental health virtual therapy with a psychologist, counselor or coach at a time and place that is convenient. If you or a loved one has suicidal thoughts or plans, call 911 right away or call or chat the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.

atoms.title: Untreated anxiety can worsen but is treatable
atoms.question: Will anxiety go away on its own?
atoms.text: It is not uncommon for people struggling with anxiety to hope it will go away on its own, but if left untreated, symptoms may get much worse. With the right combination of therapy, stress management and medication, anxiety is considered treatable.

atoms.title: Ways to help reduce anxiety
atoms.question: What are some ways to reduce anxiety?
atoms.text: Ways to help reduce anxiety include stopping what you are doing and breathing in and out slowly, eating well-balanced meals, getting enough sleep, focusing on what you can change, exercising, limiting alcohol and caffeine, and reframing negative thoughts. You can also bring yourself back to the moment with something tangible, like holding an ice cube, or redirect your energy by going for a walk.
questions: What are quick coping techniques for anxiety?

atoms.title: Types of anxiety disorders
atoms.question: What are the different types of anxiety disorders?
atoms.text: Different types of anxiety disorders exist, and knowing which type you may be dealing with can help you understand how to cope and seek help. UnitedHealthcare lists generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder (social phobia), panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and phobias.

atoms.title: 988 Lifeline for suicidal thoughts
atoms.question: Who do I call if I or a loved one has suicidal thoughts?
atoms.text: If you or a loved one has suicidal thoughts or plans, call 911 right away. The 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline is also available 24/7, providing confidential support and prevention and crisis resources. Call 988 or chat online at 988lifeline.org/chat. TTY users can use their preferred relay service or dial 711 and then 988.
